system.summary: 'Bayonne's cipher' of 1529: homophonic symbol alphabet with 2-5 signs per letter, a few nulls and word signs (roy, madame, bien, fault, paix, le Cardinal).
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's table of Bayonne's cipher (from Clair. 333, June 1530) and Friedmann's reconstruction (NAF 4206, not seen); Tomokiyo's table used and extended.
system.notes: No k/v/w; u = v. Max homophones from the NOTES table (a has five signs, s and u/v four). unread_groups = three signs on p. 21 not seen on pp. 25-27. key_order 'random' is inferred from the sign table, not stated in NOTES.

prior_solution.where: Le Grand 1688 (1529 letters incl. 30 June), Bourrilly and de Vaissiere 1905 (28 Oct 1528), Scheurer 1969 t. I (16 June 1529 block p. 41; 22 Oct 1529 opening pp. 111-112)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: DECODE record pages with login cookie

solution.what: Gallica IIIF for fr. 3077/3078; connections dropped and 429s, only fr. 3078 pp. 21-27, 31-32 (later 113-117, 133-134) at full size.
Dated the notice items against Le Grand 1688, L&P IV and Bourrilly 1905: all five catalogue letters are in print in clear.
Re-derived the key from the 22 June letter's interlinear decipherment, extending Tomokiyo's table (B = o, word signs bien, fault, paix).
Read the 16 June 1529 block (p. 21) in stretches, about 60 % of signs.
Key read the opening of the 17 Oct letter from the leaf, matching Le Grand; boxed cross = le Cardinal.
DECODE with login cookie: record pages and images for R3688-R3693, R4229; R9467 (Friedmann key) has no image attached; no DOC transcriptions on any record. Gallica IIIF/SRU 403 (Cloudflare).
DECODE harvest swept for du Bellay/Bayonne, fr. 3040/3077/3078/3005, Clair. 328-333, NAF 4206: R4229 fr. 3040 f. 68 = 30 June 1529, printed by Le Grand III 333 ff., L&P IV 5742.
p. 21 cipher block re-transcribed sign by sign from DECODE's high-resolution crop (194 signs, p21_signs.txt).

Deciphered lines 0-6 of p. 21 with the re-derived key plus Tomokiyo's table: 'si vous trouvez bon l'advis que piecza vous ay envoe de faire semblant que madame ne fust allee pour conclure et qu'estant la [?] luy ayt par importunite [R] envoye querir pouoir il ne [?] faudroyt oublier a le faire dater de ce temps la et du lieu'; fixed x-over-x = l, bracket = q, triangle-on-cross = i, diamond family m/t/n.

Scheurer t. I (1969) found through Google Books snippets: no. 12 p. 41 prints the 16 June block in clear, agreeing with the leaf reading; supplies vous, faict, madame Marguerite and 'ou sera le Roy'. Pp. 111-112 print the 22 Oct 1529 opening called undeciphered by Le Grand and L&P.
Leaf reading compared word by word with Scheurer p. 41: all words agree; signs give 'estant la' where the snippet has 'ostant'; 164 of 167 signs counted as valued (98.2%; recounted below).

Recount for the write-up: the measure had skipped line 6 (it opens with '=', read as a comment marker). Lines labelled L0-L7; 194 signs, 191 with an established value (98.5%). Before Scheurer, lines 0-6 (181 signs) had all but four values (null, vous, faict, boxed cross).

outcome.method_basis: Every cipher passage of the catalogue item is printed in clear (Le Grand 1688; Bourrilly and de Vaissiere 1905), and so are the two by-products once thought unread: the 16 June 1529 block (Scheurer 1969 no. 12 p. 41) and the 22 Oct 1529 opening (Scheurer pp. 111-112). The project re-derived the key from the 22 June interlinear and deciphered lines 0-6 of the 16 June block from the leaf before finding Scheurer, who confirmed it.
outcome.notes: 16 June 1529 block: 194 signs, 191 with an established value (98.5%), all plaintext words read and matching Scheurer; three isolated signs in line 7 unexplained. Catalogue item found already solved; R4229 (30 June 1529) also in print. Open question: the boxed cross is 'madame Marguerite' on p. 21 (Scheurer) but lined up with 'le Cardinal' on p. 113; one sign or two not settled.
outcome.fraction_read_source: p21_signs.txt (191 of 194 signs with an established value; the 16 June block only)
